q: In the year King Uzziah died, what did Isaiah see?
quote: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted

q: In Isaiah's vision of the Lord's throne, how many wings did each seraph have?
why: They covered faces and feet, and flew.
quote: Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings

q: In Isaiah's vision, what did the seraphim call out about the LORD?
why: The earth is full of His glory.
quote: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.

q: Seeing the LORD on His throne, what did Isaiah cry?
why: He knew his lips were unclean.
quote: Woe is me, for I am ruined

q: In Isaiah's vision, what did a seraph bring from the altar?
quote: and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.

q: In Isaiah's vision, where did the seraph touch him with the coal?
quote: And with it he touched my mouth

q: When the Lord asked, “Whom shall I send?” what did Isaiah answer?
quote: And I said: “Here am I. Send me!”

q: In Isaiah's sign, the virgin's son would be called what?
quote: and will call Him Immanuel.

q: Isaiah says the Lord will give a sign: who will give birth to a son?
why: Matthew says this was fulfilled in Jesus.
quote: Behold, the virgin will be with child and will give birth to a son

q: In Isaiah, what have the people walking in darkness seen?
quote: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light

q: Isaiah says, “For unto us a child is born, unto us a…”
why: The government will be on His shoulders.
quote: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given

q: In Isaiah's prophecy of the child, which is one of His names?
quote: And He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

q: In Isaiah's prophecy, on whose throne will the promised child reign?
why: His kingdom will have no end.
quote: He will reign on the throne of David and over his kingdom

q: In Isaiah's prophecy, of the increase of the child's government and peace there will be what?
quote: Of the increase of His government and peace there will be no end.

q: In Isaiah, the suffering Servant is called a man of what?
quote: He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief.

q: In Isaiah, for what was the suffering Servant pierced?
quote: But He was pierced for our transgressions

q: In Isaiah, by the suffering Servant's stripes we are what?
quote: and by His stripes we are healed.

q: In Isaiah, we all like what have gone astray?
why: Each turned to his own way.
quote: We all like sheep have gone astray

q: In Isaiah, the suffering Servant was led like what to the slaughter?
why: He did not open His mouth.
quote: He was led like a lamb to the slaughter

q: In Isaiah, what did the suffering Servant do when oppressed?
why: He was silent like a sheep.
quote: He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth.

q: In Isaiah, what did the suffering Servant carry for us?
quote: Surely He took on our infirmities and carried our sorrows

q: In Isaiah, though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as what?
quote: Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow

q: In Isaiah's vision of peace, what will nations beat their swords into?
quote: They will beat their swords into plowshares

q: In Isaiah, from whose stump will a shoot spring up?
quote: Then a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse

q: In Isaiah's vision of peace, the wolf will live with what?
why: A little child will lead them.
quote: The wolf will live with the lamb

q: In Isaiah, the LORD GOD is my strength and my what?
quote: For the LORD GOD is my strength and my song

q: In Isaiah, whom will God keep in perfect peace?
quote: You will keep in perfect peace the steadfast of mind, because he trusts in You.

q: In Isaiah, what does the voice calling in the wilderness say?
a: Prepare the way for the LORD
quote: Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness

q: In Isaiah, the grass withers, but what stands forever?
quote: The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God stands forever.

q: In Isaiah, those who wait on the LORD will mount up with wings like what?
quote: they will mount up with wings like eagles

q: In Isaiah, why does God tell His people not to fear?
quote: Do not fear, for I am with you

q: In Isaiah, God tells Israel, “I have called you by your…”
quote: I have called you by your name; you are Mine!

q: In Isaiah, God's ways are higher than ours as the heavens are higher than what?
why: His thoughts are not our thoughts.
quote: For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways

q: In Isaiah, if we are the clay, what is God?
why: We are the work of His hand.
quote: we are the clay, and You are the potter

q: In Isaiah, the Spirit-anointed one preaches good news to whom?
quote: because the LORD has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor.

q: Who was the prophet Isaiah's father?
quote: that Isaiah son of Amoz saw

q: What was the name of the son Isaiah took to meet King Ahaz?
why: They met at the upper pool.
quote: Go out with your son Shear-jashub to meet Ahaz

q: In Isaiah, which king does God call “My shepherd”?
why: He would let Jerusalem be rebuilt.
quote: who says of Cyrus, ‘My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire,’

q: In Isaiah, where does God say He has inscribed His people?
a: On the palms of His hands
quote: Behold, I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands

q: Which Assyrian king attacked Judah's cities in Hezekiah's reign?
quote: Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.

q: In Isaiah, the suffering Servant was assigned a grave with the wicked and with whom in death?
why: Jesus was buried in a rich man's tomb.
quote: and with a rich man in His death

q: In Isaiah's vision, the lame will leap like what?
why: Streams will flow in the desert.
quote: Then the lame will leap like a deer

q: In Isaiah, God says He will comfort His people as who comforts her son?
quote: As a mother comforts her son, so will I comfort you

q: In Isaiah, which region is called Galilee of the what?
quote: Galilee of the nations
